criteria.descriptor: Full marks: correctly describes temperature as logit scaling before softmax (sharpen/flatten/greedy), top-k as fixed-count truncation and top-p as adaptive cumulative-mass truncation, and correctly separates reshaping from truncation. No false claims (e.g. does not say temperature removes tokens, does not conflate top-k with top-p, and correctly qualifies temperature=0 determinism). Deduct for each mechanistic error or unqualified claim that temperature=0 is fully reproducible.

Full marks: addresses all required parts -- mechanism of all three parameters, their interaction, the diagnosis of both observed symptoms, concrete settings for BOTH subsystems, and the determinism verdict. Partial credit loses a point per omitted part (e.g. only recommends settings for one subsystem, or skips the interaction, or ignores the determinism question).

Full marks: settings are justified by the mechanism (e.g. 'top_p<1 clips the tail that high temperature inflated', 'extraction needs no sampling so temperature=0 plus constrained decoding'), not asserted as recipes. The determinism caveat is grounded in a real cause (FP non-associativity / batching / hardware). Partial credit for correct settings with thin or hand-wavy justification.

Full marks: well-organised, uses correct terminology (logits, softmax, nucleus, truncation, greedy) precisely, and clearly separates the two subsystems' recommendations. Deduct for muddled structure, vague wording, or terminology used loosely enough to obscure the mechanism.

expected_answer_points: Temperature divides the logits before softmax: T<1 sharpens toward high-probability tokens, T>1 flattens and raises the long tail, T->0 approaches greedy/argmax; it reshapes probabilities but does not remove any candidate token.

Top-k keeps a fixed number k of the most probable tokens, while top-p (nucleus) keeps the smallest set whose cumulative probability reaches p and renormalizes -- an adaptive truncation; top_p=1.0 means no truncation.

Correctly distinguishes temperature (reshaping the distribution) from top-k/top-p (truncating the candidate set) and notes they compose: truncation bounds the tail regardless of how much temperature inflated it.

Diagnoses that temperature=1.5 with top_p=1.0 flattens the distribution while leaving the full tail eligible, so rare/incoherent tokens get sampled (drafts veer off) and structure-breaking tokens slip into the extractor.

Recommends temperature=0 (greedy), ideally with constrained/structured or JSON-schema decoding, for the reproducible extraction step, because sampling variety is undesirable there and prompting alone does not guarantee valid structure.
Recommends moderate temperature (~0.7-0.9) plus a bounded top_p (~0.9) or top_k for the drafter, to keep variety while clipping the incoherent tail, rather than temperature=1.5 with full nucleus.

States that temperature=0 is near-deterministic but not guaranteed reproducible due to floating-point non-associativity, batch/kernel/hardware variation, and possible MoE routing effects; a fixed seed helps but does not fully guarantee it.
common_pitfalls: Claiming temperature=0 is fully deterministic and reproducible, ignoring floating-point non-associativity, batch composition, kernel/hardware differences, and MoE routing that can flip a near-tie argmax.
Conflating top-k and top-p, e.g. describing top-p as keeping a fixed number of tokens rather than an adaptive cumulative-probability cutoff, or thinking they are redundant knobs.
Saying temperature truncates or removes low-probability tokens; in fact it only reshapes the distribution, and truncation is the job of top-k/top-p (so top_p=1.0 leaves the whole tail samplable).
Treating higher temperature as simply 'more creative/better' without recognising that a flattened distribution plus an untruncated tail is exactly what samples rare, incoherent tokens.
Recommending the same or a high temperature for the extraction step, or assuming sampling parameters alone can fix malformed JSON instead of using temperature=0 with constrained/structured decoding.
Recommending temperature=1.5 be kept but 'add top_k later' without explaining that bounding the tail (top_p<1 or top_k) is the actual fix for the incoherent-token symptom.
reference_answer:
Temperature rescales the logits before softmax: each logit is divided by T. T<1 sharpens the distribution toward the highest-probability tokens; T>1 flattens it, pulling probability mass into the long tail of unlikely tokens; T->0 collapses to argmax (greedy). Crucially, temperature only reshapes the probabilities of ALL tokens -- it never removes any candidate.

Top-k and top-p are truncation steps that clip the candidate set before sampling. Top-k keeps the k most probable tokens (fixed count). Top-p (nucleus) keeps the smallest set of tokens whose cumulative probability reaches p, then renormalizes -- an adaptive cutoff that shrinks when the model is confident and widens when it is unsure. So temperature decides the SHAPE of the distribution; top-k/top-p decide how much of the tail you allow to be sampled from.

Diagnosis: temperature=1.5 flattens the distribution, and top_p=1.0 disables truncation, so the entire tail stays eligible. The drafter can therefore sample rare, incoherent tokens -- the 'off the rails' symptom. For extraction, that same flattening plus intact tail lets it pick tokens that break the JSON structure, giving malformed output; extraction should not be sampling creatively at all.

Recommendation: For extraction, use temperature=0 (greedy) -- ideally combined with constrained/structured decoding or a JSON/schema mode -- so structure is enforced rather than hoped for. For the drafter, keep variety but bound the tail: moderate temperature (~0.7-0.9) with top_p~0.9 (or a top_k), not temperature=1.5 with full nucleus. This gives diversity while clipping the incoherent tail.

Determinism: temperature=0 makes decoding greedy and near-deterministic, but not guaranteed bit-for-bit reproducible. Floating-point non-associativity in parallel GPU reductions, varying batch composition, kernel/hardware differences, and MoE routing can flip a near-tie argmax, so identical inputs can occasionally diverge. Pin a seed where the API supports it, but treat 'deterministic' as 'strongly reproducible, not guaranteed'.
